title: The Impact of Credit Market Development on Auditor Choice: Evidence from Banking Deregulation

scopes.description: The supplied SAS program prepares the author-described firm-year panel, builds and exports both ten-cohort stacked DiD datasets, and the supplied Stata program runs the INDEXP and BIGN regression branches. The package contains only a firm-identifier DTA, not an analysis panel; full-pipeline input and software compatibility remain unresolved.

issues.description: The supplied workflow requires twelve distinct external SAS inputs and the package contains none of those panels. Exact frozen-catalog checks and bounded one-row probes found partial local candidates for Compustat, segments, Audit Analytics, IBES and identifiers, but did not establish full author-table schemas or historical coverage. The prepared historical-state and auditor-key tables have no verified route; the direct Compustat core and restatement field requests did not validate. BLS LAUS is a documented public route; Census PEP vintage/schema coverage remains unresolved.
The SAS exports and Stata imports use matching Windows [redacted-path-772efb4f8251] paths. Map the SAS library and both DTA handoffs to one writable host-visible working root before a future run.

Stata 18 is available, but the installed SAS startup probe failed while initializing TKELS, so SAS runtime and the component needed for PROC REG remain unverified. This startup failure does not establish a missing license or component.

evidence.description: The datasheet specifies Compustat North America firm-years from 1988–2010 to supply lagged regression variables.
evidence.quote:
retrieving all the firm-years in Compustat North America for the period from 1988 to
2010 because we need the lagged value of some of the variables in the regressions. We
exclude firms that are incorporated outside of the U.S., firms in the financial and utility
sectors, and those observations with missing data on the variables in our regressions.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes the historical-headquarters-state input and its EDGAR/Compact Disclosure provenance.
evidence.quote:
Our identification strategy requires the historical state of incorporation information
for our sample firms. Because Compustat backfills its headquarters location data with
the most recent location, we collect the historical headquarters state information from
the SEC’s EDGAR database and Compact Disclosure for some of the earliest years
(similar to Dou et al. [2016]). Table 1 Panel B provides details on the sample selection

evidence.description: The datasheet names Compustat, EDGAR/Compact Disclosure, Rice–Strahan, Census and BLS as historical sample inputs.
evidence.quote:
The full firm-year sample has been generated by merging the following databases:
firm-level information from Compustat North America (initially downloaded in March
2017, and the last update was made in March 2023), historical headquarters information
from EDGAR and Compact Disclosure (obtained in November 2017), bank
deregulation event information from Rice and Strahan (2010), and state-level
information from Census Bureau (downloaded in September 2021) and the Bureau of
Labor Statistics (downloaded in January 2021).

evidence.description: The datasheet assigns preparation to SAS, regressions to Stata, and describes the DTA as firm identifiers.
evidence.quote:
Computer programs to convert the raw data into the dataset used in the analysis and a
brief description that enables other researchers to use this program are provided in the
file “BDAC SAS program.sas”, and the programs to run regressions are provided in the
file “BDAC Stata program.do”. Identifiers of firms in the firm-year sample are provided
in the file “BDAC Identifiers.dta”.

evidence.description: The SAS data-step body reads Compustat and applies U.S., financial-sector and utility exclusions.
The SAS program reads bank.rawdata1 and sorts it by CIK and fiscal year.
The SAS program joins the Audit Analytics table to the firm panel by company key and fiscal year.
The SAS program reads the historical-state table and renames its state field.
The SAS program joins historical/current state by firm and year and creates rawdata3.
The SAS program reads segment data and selects business segments.
The SAS program joins business and geographic segment counts into rawdata5.
The SAS program reads state unemployment and joins it by state and derived year-month.
The SAS program transforms and joins annual state population by state identifier and year.
The SAS program reads IBES actual/estimate fields and calculates forecast error.
The SAS program reads SEDOL mappings and derives a calendar year from datadate.
The SAS program reads the U.S. CUSIP mapping and takes its first seven characters.
The SAS program joins firm-years to SEDOL and then IBES using the seven-character identifier and year.
The SAS program reads the auditor-key table.
The SAS program joins auditor keys by firm and year and creates rawdata6.
The SAS program reads and joins going-concern observations by company key and fiscal-year-of-operation.
The SAS program reads restatement data and joins it by company and fiscal year.
The SAS program computes 1st/99th percentile cutoffs and applies them to the full filtered panel.
The SAS program creates one-row firm lags before restricting fiscal years to 1989–2010.
The SAS program estimates the accrual model with PROC REG to create residuals.
The SAS program creates the INDEXP stacked cohort dataset and exports dataindexp.dta.
The SAS program creates the BIGN stacked cohort dataset and exports databign.dta.
The Stata program loads dataindexp.dta and runs four INDEXP regressions.

actions.description: Resolve a compatible source route and author-compatible fields/history for each consumed input while retaining the supplied SAS-to-Stata workflow.
steps: For Compustat, obtain or construct an author-compatible annual panel for 1988–2010; map the supplied CIK, fiscal year, location and SIC fields, verify every consumed accounting column, and retain the preceding firm-year used by the lag step.

Treat FEED03, FEED34 and FEED39 as feed-level Audit Analytics candidates, not as the complete author tables. Obtain or construct compatible audit, going-concern and restatement inputs with the exact supplied company/fiscal-year joins and flag semantics.

Obtain the author-prepared historicalstate and auditorkey tables or a documented compatible equivalent keyed by gvkey/year. The datasheet's EDGAR/Compact Disclosure provenance alone does not require raw filing reconstruction.

Acquire BLS LAUS monthly state unemployment-rate series for the required years and map state, month and rate to the supplied state/yearmonth/ur join; preserve the author's historical vintage if an available official series supports it.

Identify and acquire a compatible Census PEP historical vintage of annual July 1 state population estimates; verify 1989–2010 coverage and map its state key/year/population to the supplied stateid/year/population fields.

Confirm that the chosen IBES US EPS summary variant covers the required forecast-period years and supports the supplied ticker/CUSIP/year joins. Confirm historical SEDOL and CUSIP mappings; the probed global and North America Compustat tables are candidates only.

Keep each consumed input as a separate requirement. A compatible public, local or author-prepared alternative can satisfy its own input after its field, unit, identifier and coverage mappings are established; do not require reconstruction of unrelated historical source layers as additional inputs.
validation: After authorized staging, use bounded format-aware metadata checks to verify exact pre-conversion columns, units, keys and date ranges for each selected source; then validate join uniqueness, panel counts and required history in a separately authorized full run.
Do not infer coverage from one-row samples or catalog counts; keep the analysis period and the Compustat lag year explicit.

review_notes: Completed the assigned full_pipeline target from the exact supplied SAS and Stata programs, datasheet, inventory and all 25 frozen dependency IDs. The SAS program contains substantive construction plus separate INDEXP and BIGN stacked-cohort branches; Stata loads the two matching SAS export basenames and estimates four regressions per branch. The packaged DTA is only firm identifiers, so it does not support an analysis_only scope.

The final pre-display screen flagged SAS line 4 only; SAS lines 1–9 were withheld as one opaque block, and Stata had no candidate lines. A literal-free structural inspection established only a safe bank libref assignment and the bank.rawdata1 data-step header. Do not infer credential contents, connection behavior, or an access barrier from that screen.

Exact frozen-catalog lookups and nine one-row probes were limited to named candidate tables under ${ACCTREPL_SAS_ROOT}, through the assigned frozen CLI and registered resource helper. Probes expose schema/count metadata only, have coverage_verified=false, and do not establish history. Compustat, segments, Audit Analytics feeds, IBES and identifier candidates are not treated as complete author-prepared inputs. The FEED39 and combined FUNDA field-validation errors are schema uncertainty, not evidence that data or access are absent.

Official static BLS LAUS and Census PEP pages were inspected. BLS documents monthly state series beginning in 1976; Census documents July 1 estimates and historical vintages. No API endpoints, data payloads, or downloads were requested, so exact Census vintage/schema and the author's historical public-data values remain to be checked during authorized acquisition.

The existing environment artifact records Stata 18 available and SAS unverified after a TKELS startup failure; no author code or study data were executed. Static readiness findings do not establish successful reproduction. Both [redacted-path-b03a8f023939] filename pairs match; the Windows root is a known portability setup task.

Process-only scanner, runner and bounded-query failures/corrections remain preserved in probes. The initial generic `python` lookup failure, scanner regex failures and broad-key over-redaction are not scientific evidence. A final-reference preflight also corrected stale evidence IDs inherited from the first draft checkpoint. The final source reader's candidate output and all listed artifact hashes are retained for coordinator source QA.

One initial BLS/Census search response exceeded the available context and one BLS static-page open returned UnexpectedStatusCode; their visible requests/errors and capture limits are retained in an unreferenced process-only inspection artifact. Later official static BLS and Census pages opened successfully. No failed lookup is used as source or access-barrier evidence.
